# ToolTip

Header: `winui/ui/dialogs/ToolTip.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/dialogs/ToolTip.hpp`.

Hover text for an element, opened after the pointer rests on the anchor and closed when the pointer leaves or clicks.

A [ToolTip](#uitooltip) wraps its anchor. It takes the anchor's place in the tree and passes layout, rendering, input, focus and automation through, so the anchor behaves as it would unwrapped. The tip content lives outside the main tree. The window lays it out and draws it on the theme's tooltip surface. The open delay counts down in [tick_override()](#tick_override), so the host must tick the [Window](../tree/window.md), as the built-in window host does. A tip opened by the mouse docks to the pointer, inflated by the offsets. For plain text on any element, [Element::set_tool_tip()](../tree/element.md#set_tool_tip) is shorter.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto  tip     = std::make_unique<ui::ToolTipControl>();
auto* save    = tip->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Save"));
tip->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Saves the current document"));
tip->set_placement(ui::PopupPlacement::Below);
save->on_click([] { save_document(); });
toolbar->add(std::move(tip)); // the ToolTip takes the Button's place in the tree

// Declaratively:
toolbar->add(ui::ToolTip{
    .anchor  = ui::Button{.text = "Save"},
    .content = ui::Text{.text = "Saves the current document"},
}.build());
```

## `ui::ToolTip`

A hover tip over an anchor. Builds a [ui::ToolTipControl](#uitooltipcontrol).

The built element wraps the anchor, which lays out and takes input as usual; the tip shows after the pointer rests on it for [`.delay`](#uitooltip-delay) and hides on a press, a key or the pointer leaving.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::ToolTip{
    .placement = ui::PopupPlacement::Below,
    .anchor    = ui::Button{ .text = "Open", .on_click = [&] { open_file(); } },
    .content   = ui::Text{ .text = "Open a document from disk" },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::ToolTip{
    .delay, .placement, .horizontal_offset, .vertical_offset, .placement_rect, .style, .margin,
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control,
    .anchor, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uitooltip-delay"></span>`delay` | `ui::Binding<ui::Duration>` | `{ui::Duration{800.0}}` | How long the pointer must rest on the anchor before the tip opens; 800 ms by default. |
| <span id="uitooltip-placement"></span>`placement` | `ui::Binding<ui::PopupPlacement>` | `{ui::PopupPlacement::Above}` | Which side of the pointer (or [`placement_rect`](#uitooltip-placement_rect)) the tip sits on. |
| <span id="uitooltip-horizontal_offset"></span>`horizontal_offset` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{20.0f}` | How far the dock rect is inflated on the left and right, in DIPs. |
| <span id="uitooltip-vertical_offset"></span>`vertical_offset` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{20.0f}` | How far the dock rect is inflated on the top and bottom, in DIPs. |
| <span id="uitooltip-placement_rect"></span>`placement_rect` | `ui::Binding<std::optional<ui::Rect>>` |  | A rect in the anchor's coordinates to dock to instead of the pointer. |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uitooltip-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uitooltip-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::ToolTip>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uitooltip-anchor"></span>`anchor` | `ui::Spec` |  | The element the tip belongs to; it takes the [ToolTip](#uitooltip)'s place in the layout. |
| <span id="uitooltip-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | What the tip shows, usually a [ui::Text](text.md#uitext). |

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::ToolTipControl](#uitooltipcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::ToolTipControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

Hover text for an element, opened after the pointer rests on the anchor and closed when the pointer leaves or clicks.

A [ToolTip](#uitooltip) wraps its anchor. It takes the anchor's place in the tree and passes layout, rendering, input, focus and automation through, so the anchor behaves as it would unwrapped. The tip content lives outside the main tree. The window lays it out and draws it on the theme's tooltip surface. The open delay counts down in [tick_override()](#tick_override), so the host must tick the [Window](../tree/window.md), as the built-in window host does. A tip opened by the mouse docks to the pointer, inflated by the offsets. For plain text on any element, [Element::set_tool_tip()](../tree/element.md#set_tool_tip) is shorter.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  toolbar = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto  tip     = std::make_unique<ui::ToolTipControl>();
auto* save    = tip->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Save"));
tip->set_content(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Saves the current document"));
tip->set_placement(ui::PopupPlacement::Below);
save->on_click([] { save_document(); });
toolbar->add(std::move(tip)); // the ToolTip takes the Button's place in the tree

// Declaratively:
toolbar->add(ui::ToolTip{
    .anchor  = ui::Button{.text = "Save"},
    .content = ui::Text{.text = "Saves the current document"},
}.build());
```

### ToolTipControl

```cpp
ToolTipControl() = default
```

An empty tooltip: no anchor, no content, 800 ms delay, placed Above.

### set_anchor

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_anchor(std::unique_ptr<T> anchor)
```

Takes ownership of the anchor element, the element the tip describes, and returns a non-owning observer, as [FlyoutControl::set_anchor()](flyout.md#set_anchor) and [ScrollControl::set_child()](../layout/scroll.md#set_child) do. Replaces and destroys any previous anchor.

### anchor

```cpp
Element* anchor() const
```

The anchor, or null before [set_anchor()](#set_anchor). Owned by this [ToolTip](#uitooltip).

### set_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_content(std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

Takes ownership of the floating hover content and returns a non-owning observer. The content is not part of the main tree. The window lays it out and draws it separately. The tooltip's background, border and padding come from the theme, so the content needs none.

### content

```cpp
Element* content() const
```

The floating content, or null before [set_content()](#set_content). Owned by this [ToolTip](#uitooltip).

### is_open

```cpp
bool is_open() const
```

Whether the tip is showing. It opens once the hover delay elapses or [show_at()](#show_at) is called. It closes when the pointer leaves, on a click, on [close()](#close), or when the popup is dismissed.

### delay

```cpp
Duration delay() const
```

How long the pointer must stay over the anchor before the tooltip opens; 800 ms by default.

### set_delay

```cpp
void set_delay(Duration delay)
```

Sets the delay. It also applies to a countdown already running, which keeps its elapsed time.

### placement

```cpp
PopupPlacement placement() const
```

Which side of the dock rect the tooltip opens against; Above by default. It flips to Below near the top edge of the window.

### set_placement

```cpp
void set_placement(PopupPlacement placement)
```

Sets the side. Takes effect the next time the popup is placed.

### horizontal_offset

```cpp
float horizontal_offset() const
```

How far the dock rect is inflated on the left and right before the tooltip is placed against it, in DIPs; 20 by default. [vertical_offset()](#vertical_offset) does the same for the top and bottom.

### set_horizontal_offset

```cpp
void set_horizontal_offset(float offset)
```

Sets the horizontal inflation in DIPs. A negative value shrinks the dock rect, pulling the tip over it.

### vertical_offset

```cpp
float vertical_offset() const
```

The vertical inflation in DIPs; 20 by default. See [horizontal_offset()](#horizontal_offset).

### set_vertical_offset

```cpp
void set_vertical_offset(float offset)
```

Sets the vertical inflation in DIPs.

### placement_rect

```cpp
const std::optional<Rect>& placement_rect() const
```

The placement rect, in the anchor's own coordinates. The tooltip docks to it instead of the pointer, so it opens beside the rect and doesn't cover what it describes.

### set_placement_rect

```cpp
void set_placement_rect(std::optional<Rect> rect)
```

Sets or clears the placement rect. nullopt docks to the pointer again.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Focusable exactly when the anchor is; focus itself goes to the anchor.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

The anchor, if any. The tip's content is popup content, outside the tree.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

The tip stands in for its anchor as one tab stop. Focus itself goes to the anchor.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>&) const override
```

No automation children: the anchor is not listed under the tip.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

The anchor's role, name and providers, so screen readers see the anchor. With no anchor, a Group with nothing to act on.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

[automation_name()](../tree/element.md#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

### show_at

```cpp
void show_at(Point pointer)
```

Opens the tip now, docked to `pointer` (window DIPs) as a tip opened by the mouse is, whatever the pointer does over the anchor. The window shows [Element::set_tool_tip()](../tree/element.md#set_tool_tip) text this way. Calling it while open moves the dock point.

### close

```cpp
void close()
```

Closes the tip and resets the hover countdown. Nothing changes on screen when it is already closed.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Forwards every event to the anchor and tracks hover. A move starts the countdown, leaving cancels it or closes the tip, and a press closes the tip.

### handled_pointer_override

```cpp
void handled_pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A press the anchor took closes the tip too.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Ticks the anchor, then advances the hover countdown and opens the tip once it reaches [delay()](#delay).

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### text_override

```cpp
bool text_override(const TextInputEvent& text_event) override
```

Typed text for this element, routed like [key_override()](#key_override). Default: false.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_visible_changed

```cpp
void focus_visible_changed(bool visible) override
```

[focus_visible()](../tree/element.md#focus_visible) changed; the element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### draws_focus_ring

```cpp
bool draws_focus_ring() const override
```

None of its own: the anchor inside it draws its own focus ring.
